comment: WHICH REVIEWER OWES A VERDICT ON WHICH DIFF, as data a machine can evaluate. Every reviewer's frontmatter `description` already says this in prose — 'MUST BE USED after any change to supabase/migrations/**, ... or server-side auth verification' — and eight of those declarations existed for five releases with NOTHING anywhere reading a transcript, hooking SubagentStop, or otherwise observing that any reviewer ran. The harness enforced what a reviewer FILE says (frontmatter parses, tools are a read-only subset, the body ends demanding VERDICT: PASS|BLOCK, the whole surface sha-locked in tools/agents.lock.json) and nothing about whether it RAN. This file is the trigger half moved out of prose; .claude/hooks/subagent-verdict.mjs records the verdicts; tools/check-reviewer-verdicts.mjs is the Stop step that judges one against the other. THE PATTERNS ARE DELIBERATELY NARROWER THAN THE PROSE. A trigger that over-matches makes every diff owe every reviewer, and a gate that fires on everything is one people learn to route around — which is worse than the prose it replaced. When in doubt, leave a path out and widen it in a reviewed diff. SOURCE: template/base/.claude/agents/*.md (the `description` each pattern set is derived from) · CHANGELOG 0.3.0 (process-verified reviewers, deferred with the reason)
matching: A pattern is a POSIX-style glob over a repo-relative path: `*` matches within one segment, `**` matches across segments. Matching is case-sensitive. A reviewer is OWED a verdict when any changed path matches any of its patterns and no `except` pattern matches that same path.

reviewers.why: RLS keyed on auth.uid() IS the authorization boundary, and it is the one surface where a mistake is invisible in review and total in production. The paths are the ones where a policy, a grant, or the server-side identity check can change.
reviewers.exceptWhy: A test file next to a policy is not itself a policy. Excluding them keeps the trigger on the surface that carries the authorization decision — a reviewer summoned by a test edit is the noise that teaches people to skip the reviewer that matters.

reviewers.why: The web half has its own failure modes the Supabase reviewer does not look for: a Server Action that trusts its input, a module-scope client leaking one request's identity into another's render, proxy.ts mistaken for an authorization boundary (CVE-2025-29927), and NEXT_PUBLIC_ names that inline into the shipped bundle.

The native config surface is the one an ordinary diff cannot show the consequences of: a permission string, an ATS exception or a runtimeVersion policy reads as one line and changes what the store ships and what the OS allows.

The a11y floor is lint plus component tests by the gates-catalog's own admission, and the EAA makes that a legal exposure rather than a quality gap. A human read of a UI diff is the compensating control, so it has to be observed rather than requested.

The anatomy laws (boundaries part 3) hold the mechanical half of the worked pattern; this reviewer holds the judgment half — abstraction accounting, cohesion, naming coherence, special-casing — on the structural surface where those decisions are made. Scoped to packages/** and the two structural registers, deliberately NOT apps/** yet: the file's own doctrine is narrowness first, widening in a reviewed diff (register row architecture-reviewer-apps-widening tracks the widening decision against one release of verdict-ledger evidence).
reviewers.exceptWhy: A test file exercises structure; it does not create it. The reviewer is owed on the structural act, and summoning it for every test edit is the noise that teaches people to route around the reviewer that matters.

reviewers.why: AGENTS.md states in its own words that 'UI diffs end with a design-reviewer PASS'. That sentence was advisory for five releases. Same path set as the a11y reviewer because the two look at the same diff for different things.

notTriggered.why: AGENTS.md says it runs 'before finishing' — that is EVERY turn, which no diff pattern expresses and which a path trigger would model badly. Making it path-triggered would either fire it on everything (noise) or on an arbitrary subset (a rule that reads as coverage and is not). Left out deliberately rather than approximated; a whole-turn obligation needs a different mechanism than a path glob.

Driven by the /verify-citations command and closed by the `provenance` chain gate, which reds tree-wide on an uncited decision site. It already has a deterministic control; adding a second, weaker one keyed on paths would let a green path-trigger imply a coverage the gate is the real source of.
An AUTHOR, not a reviewer. It produces the diff; it does not attest to one. Its output is judged by the same gates as any other code.
An author, for the same reason. `security-reviewer` is the one that must attest to what it wrote.
An author. `check-test-quality.mjs` and the mutation ratchet are what judge its output, and both are deterministic.
